relations.subject: ahuzzath
relations.note: Named friendship in Isaac’s episode only; no identity with earlier royal entourage is inferred.

relations.subject: hirah
relations.note: Explicitly identified as Judah’s friend, not a co-occurrence association.

relations.subject: potiphera
relations.note: Priesthood role associated with the named place On; Potiphera is not Potiphar.

relations.subject: isaac
relations.note: Isaac is the contextual naming subject; servants dug the well. This edge does not credit him with solitary digging.

relations.subject: isaac
relations.note: The named individual continues as the naming subject; the plural digging party is not collapsed into Isaac as sole builder.

relations.subject: isaac
relations.note: Names the specific well Rehoboth, not other Rehoboth places or their builders.

relations.subject: jacob
relations.note: Naming act is narrated; the identity of the angels is not resolved.

relations.subject: jacob
relations.note: Naming is narrated. Jacob’s explanation about seeing God is speech, not an identity equation between the wrestler and God.

relations.subject: jacob
relations.note: Names the heap Galeed; its alias Jegar Sahadutha is Laban’s naming of the same heap. Does not ascribe sole construction to Jacob.

relations.subject: jacob
relations.note: Jacob’s pitched tent is explicitly located by the narrative; no modern mountain coordinates are asserted.

relations.subject: jacob
relations.note: Context identifies Jacob, who crosses the ford with his family; not an assertion that he crossed alone.

relations.subject: tamar
relations.note: Records her sitting at the gate, not a claim that she was a prostitute or a permanent resident.

relations.subject: rachel
relations.note: Route-relative burial location only; it is explicitly not an assertion of burial inside Bethlehem.

relations.subject: jacob
relations.note: Jacob sends messengers toward Esau in the land of Seir, field of Edom. Person Esau and territory Edom remain distinct; no identity/modern-border claim.

relations.subject: jacob
relations.note: Jacob is the explicitly identified father among the family Joseph settles in Rameses. This contextual individual participation does not equate Rameses with Goshen or a later city.

relations.subject: joseph
relations.note: Joseph is explicitly named as leading/participating in the funeral party that arrives at Atad; this is a shared journey, not an assertion that he traveled alone.

relations.subject: deborah-rebekah
relations.note: Explicit household role named in the verse, without inferring later servant identities.

relations.subject: hamor
relations.note: Hamor goes to Jacob to discuss the proposed marriage; this does not assert that the marriage took place or assign individual agents to the later joint killings.

relations.subject: laban
relations.note: Laban names the heap Jegar Sahadutha, an explicit alias of the heap Jacob calls Galeed.

relations.subject: laban
relations.note: Laban and his relatives encamp there; not a solitary journey.

relations.subject: hirah
relations.note: Hirah accompanies Judah to the sheep shearers; a shared journey with explicit named participants.

friend_of.description: Explicitly named friendship, stored once; not inferred from proximity.

priest_of.description: Person serving as priest of the named place; no identification of the worshipped deity is implied.

named.description: Narrated naming of a place or object; the assigned name is in entity aliases and evidence. Does not imply sole construction.

camped_at.description: Temporary encampment at the cited textual place, including explicit group participation.

crossed.description: Narrated crossing of a named watercourse/ford; no modern route reconstructed.

waited_at.description: Person sits/waits at named place; not permanent residence or an occupation.

buried_on_way_to.description: Route-relative burial; explicitly not burial inside the destination town.

sent_messengers_to.description: Sender dispatches messengers toward named location; does not establish sender arrival.

nurse_of.description: Explicit nurse/household-care role; does not infer biological motherhood.
